DORSET DIVISION / LEGAL

Deposits & Payments

Last updated: 25 October 2026

Agree the cost first

Your written quote or proposal confirms what is included, the total price or agreed calculation method, payment dates and approved outside costs before you commit. Dorset Division is not registered for VAT and does not charge VAT. Third-party providers may charge VAT on their own services. No paid work or optional extra is added without agreement.

Deposits and staged payments

Direct fixed-price projects normally use a 50% deposit and 50% final payment unless a different schedule is expressly agreed in the quote. Smaller tasks, retainers or larger projects may use a different arrangement. A deposit forms part of the total project price; it is not an extra fee. Work is scheduled after acceptance and receipt of the agreed initial payment, subject to your consumer rights.

What happens to a deposit

A deposit may cover reserved time, planning and initial work. It is not automatically non-refundable. If work ends early, I will explain any proposed deduction by reference to the agreement, work actually supplied, reasonable unavoidable losses and applicable law. You will not be charged twice for the same loss. See Cancellations & Refunds.

Invoices and final delivery

Please pay using the method and reference on your invoice. The invoice and proposal set the due date; there is no hidden default payment period. Final handover, launch or transfer may depend on the agreed balance being paid where this has been clearly agreed and is lawful. Please raise an invoice query promptly; disputed amounts will be reviewed fairly.

Extra work and expenses

Work outside the agreed scope requires written approval of the additional cost and timetable. Domains, hosting, paid apps, subscriptions, advertising, printing, stock assets and other third-party services are separate unless expressly included. Their ownership, renewals and ongoing costs should be clear in the quote.

Retainers and marketplace work

Ongoing work will have an agreed scope or time allowance, billing cycle and notice arrangement. There is no automatic renewal or minimum term unless expressly agreed. PeoplePerHour projects normally keep payments on PeoplePerHour and follow its agreed milestones and platform rules.

Overdue payments

If a payment is overdue, I will contact you before considering a reasonable pause in further work, subject to the contract and your legal rights. Any lawful interest or recovery charges must be properly notified; this page does not create an arbitrary late fee.

Payment questions

Email marnie@dorsetdivision.co.uk or telephone 07342 729185. Postal contact details are in Legal Information. Services are remote; there is no public walk-in office.

Do not enter card details, bank passwords or payment credentials in the website enquiry form, review form or Burt chat. Consumer statutory rights are not affected by this policy.
